name: EcomTrade24 Pay for WooCommerce
author: ecomtrade24

sections.description:
EcomTrade24 Pay connects your WooCommerce store to the EcomTrade24 Pay merchant platform. A free merchant account and API key are required to use this plugin.

Create a free merchant account | Integration documentation | Pricing

Features:
* Direct cryptocurrency checkout, including supported assets and networks configured for your merchant account.
* Hosted checkout for Free merchants.
* Optional Smart Routing and eligible third-party fiat-to-crypto methods on supported paid plans.
* Classic WooCommerce checkout and WooCommerce Checkout Blocks support.
* Payment session reuse, payment status synchronization and webhook handling.
* Merchant settings and connection diagnostics.

Customers may be redirected to EcomTrade24 Pay or independent on-ramp providers. Available payment methods depend on merchant configuration, buyer location, provider eligibility and transaction details. Third-party providers may require identity verification.

External services

This plugin connects to the EcomTrade24 Pay service at https://pay.ecomtrade24.com to create and track payment sessions, retrieve merchant capabilities, perform connection checks and process payment notifications. Data sent as needed for transactions can include order identifiers, amounts, currency, store domain and customer email. The six official payment-method PNG logos are downloaded from https://pay.ecomtrade24.com/assets/logos/ using the WordPress HTTP API and cached locally when available. Optional telemetry is disabled by default and only enabled when the merchant explicitly opts in under gateway settings. If enabled, it sends store URL/domain, WordPress/WooCommerce/PHP/plugin versions, enabled payment options, currency and checkout configuration approximately every 15 minutes and while checkout pages are visited. Merchants may disable this at any time without disabling payment processing. A manually requested heartbeat sends the same diagnostic information once. These requests authenticate the configured merchant and report connection / integration context. Gateway connection tests also transmit merchant configuration and diagnostic information. API credentials are used to authenticate merchant requests. Depending on the checkout route, customers may be redirected to independent payment or on-ramp providers, which apply their own terms and privacy policies.

Service: EcomTrade24 Pay (https://pay.ecomtrade24.com/). Terms of Service: https://pay.ecomtrade24.com/terms . Privacy Policy: https://pay.ecomtrade24.com/privacy . Documentation: https://pay.ecomtrade24.com/docs/ . The merchant is responsible for informing customers about payment-related data transfers.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate WooCommerce.
  2. Install and activate EcomTrade24 Pay for WooCommerce.
  3. Create a free merchant account and complete required account verification and shop configuration.
  4. Use Authorize shop and Complete connection in the WooCommerce payment settings to securely import your merchant API key and matching webhook signing secret, or configure both manually.
  5. Open WooCommerce > EcomTrade24 Pay and confirm both API key and matching signing secret are configured (minimum 24 characters).
  6. Configure your shop domain, payout wallet and webhook URL in the merchant dashboard. The webhook URL must target your WooCommerce callback. Make sure the signing secret matches the shop or merchant secret used for delivery. Unsigned webhooks are rejected.
  7. Run the API-key connection test, then place a test order to validate the session HMAC signature and ensure checkout works before accepting live payments.
sections.faq:
Do I need an account?

Yes. Sign up for a Free merchant account. A merchant API key is required.

Is the plugin free?

The plugin is free to install. Transaction service fees apply. The Free plan has no monthly subscription fee; see the current pricing.

Does it support Checkout Blocks?

Yes, it includes a Checkout Blocks integration as well as classic checkout support.

Are card payments handled by my WordPress website?

No. Optional fiat-to-crypto payments are handled through eligible third-party providers and may require identity verification.

Where can I get help?

See documentation and contact.
sections.changelog:
2.5.1

  • Corrected merchant pairing and settings handling to prevent mismatched API keys and signing secrets after credential changes.
  • Added actionable admin notices and safe WooCommerce logs for gateway checkout-signature rejections.
  • Keep signed Fiat and Crypto sessions, active-method filtering, and payment-method branding.
  • Use WordPress.org for automatic updates in the WordPress.org repository edition.

2.5.0

  • Fixed Checkout Blocks Store API payment method selection, including local Fiat on-ramp method values.
  • Enforced the gateway minimum signing-secret length and retained HMAC-SHA256 request signing for Fiat and Crypto sessions.
  • Added safely redacted diagnostics for rejected session creation and checkout exceptions.

2.4.9

  • Restore reliable admin settings via WooCommerce > EcomTrade24 Pay, with fixed high-contrast light UI.
  • Protect saved API credentials on blank-field saves and retain signed checkout.

2.4.8

  • Added dedicated WooCommerce settings for Fiat and Crypto with improved contrast and secure credential persistence.

2.4.7

  • Corrected official PayPal logo filename to paypal-original.png (download and local cache).
  • Classic and Blocks now show only Smart Routing methods explicitly enabled, configured and available in /gateway/me.php for the customer checkout context.
  • Removed disabled/greyed-out rows and all invented Card defaults; unavailable API results fail closed.
  • Added UPI/IMPS and Interac where confirmed active by the API, preserving the gateway’s method order.
  • Capability cache reduced to 30 seconds with versioned cache keys; no cross-context stale fallback.
  • Gateway branding in the fiat option no longer suggests Card is enabled when it is not.

2.4.5

  • Correct HTML-encoded gateway titles in both Classic and Blocks checkouts, including older saved settings.
  • Use the six official gateway payment PNG assets (Card, Crypto, iDEAL, Klarna, PayPal and Revolut), with WordPress HTTP downloads, local caching and secure refresh in merchant settings.
  • Replace incorrect fixed provider labels with truthful fiat-to-crypto on-ramp method labels.
  • Align Checkout Blocks with saved Smart Routing preference and merchant eligibility, and fix checkout mode persistence after saving.
  • Hide payment methods until a merchant API key is configured; disable debug logging by default for new installs and protect Apache log files.
  • Make checkout layout options and optional branding behave as configured for Classic and Blocks.
  • Remove obsolete provider-specific payment eligibility rules in favor of the gateway API response.

2.4.4

  • Restore signed checkout handoff for WooCommerce Card/local methods and signed chooser links.
  • Reuse existing order sessions using the stored secure checkout link; no duplicate payment session.
  • Keep signed checkout links out of WooCommerce debug logs.

2.4.3

  • Checkout session creation HTTP wait increased to 75 seconds to allow V3 wallet and Alchemy webhook preparation to finish.
  • Extend the PHP execution budget where permitted and the WooCommerce per-order lock lifetime to avoid parallel session creation during slow provider responses.
  • Record request durations in existing gateway debug logs.

2.4.2

  • Merchant-account pairing also imports the matching webhook signing secret used by server-side notifications.
  • Fail closed when the merchant has no signing secret configured.

2.4.1

  • WordPress.org review hardening: require signed webhooks, optional telemetry consent, opt-in checkout branding and more restrictive request sanitization.

2.4.0

  • Added secure WooCommerce merchant-account pairing with a short-lived approval flow.
  • No changes to payment processing, routing or settlement behavior.

2.3.13

  • Updated WooCommerce checkout styling and settings presentation.
  • Added merchant sign-up links and WordPress.org listing documentation.
  • Prepared distribution through WordPress.org’s update mechanism.
  • Removed alternative plugin updater and external checkout image dependencies.
  • Disabled optional public attribution links by default for new installs.
  • Avoided API credentials in crypto fallback request URLs.
